[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
William Glasgow was born in Chesham, Buckinghamshire, about 1830–1831. The 1911 census lists him as an 80-year-old Baptist minister and head of household at 34 Freehold Road, Ipswich, Suffolk.<ref>[https://www.ancestry.co.uk/search/collections/2352/records/43736903 1911 Census of England and Wales, RG 14/10842, William Glasgow], Ancestry index.</ref>

Philip Reynolds's obituary says William became pastor at Bardwell in 1875, later served at Tunstall, and retired in 1900. The obituary records his death on 6 March 1913 at age 83.<ref>[https://www.baptists.net/history/2025/03/the-life-and-death-of-william-glasgow/ Philip Reynolds, obituary of William Glasgow, ''Earthen Vessel'' (1913)].</ref> Kelly's 1892 directory lists Rev. W. Glasgow at Tunstall, near Wickham Market.<ref>[https://leicester.contentdm.oclc.org/digital/collection/p16445coll4/id/245483 ''Kelly's Directory of Cambridgeshire, Norfolk and Suffolk'' (1892), Suffolk section, Rev. W. Glasgow].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The census, Suffolk directories and obituary agree on his name, occupation and Suffolk connection. The obituary and census both identify Chesham as his birthplace. The two surviving census-based birth estimates are approximate. Two undated namesakes still lack enough detail to establish whether either is the Suffolk minister. The William Glasgow named in the Killycurragh family letter (PRONI T1959/3) had an adult son who died in 1801, before the Suffolk minister was born.
